chunks: Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about forgetfulness, so he said:

Whoever keeps track of his forgetfulness and completes it, then the two prostrations of forgetfulness are not upon him. Rather, forgetfulness applies to one who does not know whether he added to his salat (prayer) or omitted from it.

key_terms.السَّهْوِ: forgetfulness or inadvertent lapse in salat (prayer)
key_terms.سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness in salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَأَتَمَّهُ: then completes or corrects it properly
key_terms.يَحْفَظْ: keeps track of or correctly recognizes

ai.seo_question: When are the two prostrations of forgetfulness required in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding sahw in salat (prayer). If a person recognizes the lapse and properly completes the prayer, Sajdatā al-Sahw are not required; they apply to the one who remains uncertain whether he added to or omitted part of the prayer.
